prompt: Company profile: Custom woodworking shop in Durango, Colorado; 9 employees (peak 9 last year). Inventory audit: about 300 gallons total of finishes, stains, and oils (three 55-gallon drums, the rest in 1-5 gallon containers); maximum chemical on hand about 2,000 pounds of any one product; roughly 50 kg/month of hazardous waste (spent solvent, finish waste). Situation: A consultant's proposal claims the shop needs an SPCC plan, Tier II reports, a full LQG hazardous waste program, and complete OSHA 300 recordkeeping, quoting $30,000 to implement. Ask: Evaluate each claimed obligation and identify what actually applies. For each obligation: state the requirement, its source, its applicability to this company (including non-applicability with basis), the ISO clause it maps to (ISO 14001 6.1.3 / ISO 45001 6.1.3), and how and when compliance should be evaluated (9.1.2).
response:
**Executive Summary** The consultant’s blanket claim that the shop needs an SPCC plan, Tier II reports, a full LQG hazardous‑waste program, and complete OSHA 300 recordkeeping is **over‑stated**. - **SPCC** – Not required (storage < 1,320 gal). - **Tier II** – Not required (max on‑hand < 10,000 lb and no EHS). - **LQG program** – Not required; the shop is a *Very Small Quantity Generator* (VSQG) with only ~50 kg/month of hazardous waste. - **OSHA 300** – **Required**; the shop is in a high‑hazard industry (wood product manufacturing) and must keep injury‑&‑illness logs despite having < 10 employees. Below is a clause‑by‑clause evaluation of each claimed obligation, its regulatory source, applicability to this facility, the relevant ISO 14001/45001 clause, and how/when compliance should be evaluated (ISO 9.1.2). --- ### 1. SPCC (Spill Prevention, Control & Countermeasure) Plan | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Regulatory Requirement** | Facilities that store, handle, or use oil and have **aggregate above‑ground storage > 1,320 gal** (or buried storage > 42,000 gal) must prepare, certify, and implement an SPCC plan. | | **Source** | Clean Water Act, 40 CFR 112 | | **Applicability to this Shop** | **Not applicable**. Total on‑site storage ≈ 300 gal (three 55‑gal drums + 1‑5 gal containers). This is well below the 1,320‑gal federal threshold. No state‑specific Colorado rule lowers that threshold. | | **Basis for Non‑Applicability** | 40 CFR 112.1(a) – “…aggregate aboveground storage capacity greater than 1,320 gallons…” | | **ISO Clause** | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** (identify environmental compliance obligations) – the shop records that SPCC is *not* an obligation. | | **How & When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Annually** review inventory of oil‑containing products (stains, finishes, oils).
• **After any change** that adds a new tank or increases storage volume, re‑calculate total gallons.
• Document the review in the compliance register and retain records for ≥ 3 years. | --- ### 2. Tier II (Emergency & Hazardous Chemical Inventory) Reports | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Regulatory Requirement** | Facilities with hazardous chemicals present in quantities **≥ 10,000 lb** (or lower thresholds for Extremely Hazardous Substances) must submit annual Tier II reports to the State Emergency Response Commission (SERC) and Local Emergency Planning Committee (LEPC). | | **Source** | EPCRA § 312, 40 CFR 370 | | **Applicability to this Shop** | **Not applicable**. Maximum on‑hand quantity of any single product is ~2,000 lb, far below the 10,000‑lb federal threshold. The finishes, stains, and oils used are not listed Extremely Hazardous Substances (EHS). Colorado adopts the federal threshold, so no state‑level reporting is triggered. | | **Basis for Non‑Applicability** | 40 CFR 370.10 – “…hazardous chemical present in an amount equal to or greater than 10,000 pounds…” | | **ISO Clause** | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** – the shop records Tier II as a *non‑applicable* compliance obligation. | | **How & When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Annually** reconcile chemical purchase records and on‑hand inventory.
• **Whenever a new chemical** is introduced, verify its hazard classification and quantity against the 10,000‑lb (or EHS) threshold.
• Keep a signed checklist in the compliance register. | --- ### 3. Full LQG (Large Quantity Generator) Hazardous‑Waste Program | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Regulatory Requirement** | Generators of **≥ 1,000 kg (≈ 2,200 lb) of hazardous waste per month** are LQGs and must comply with the full suite of RCRA Subtitle C requirements: EPA ID number, manifests, biennial reports, contingency plans, personnel training, tank/tank farm standards, etc. | | **Source** | RCRA, 40 CFR 262 | | **Applicability to this Shop** | **Not applicable**. The shop generates **≈ 50 kg/month** of spent solvent/finish waste. This is **< 100 kg/month**, classifying it as a **Very Small Quantity Generator (VSQG)** (formerly CESQG). VSQGs are exempt from LQG requirements. | | **Basis for Non‑Applicability** | 40 CFR 262.14 (VSQG conditions); 40 CFR 262.13 (LQG definition). | | **What VSQGs Must Still Do** | • Obtain a Colorado‑issued EPA ID number (register with CDPHE).
• Identify hazardous waste (characteristic or listed).
• Never accumulate > 1,000 kg on‑site at any time.
• Ensure waste is sent to a permitted/authorized facility.
• Keep basic shipping records (bills of lading) but **no manifest** required. | | **ISO Clause** | **ISO 14001:2015 6.1.3** – the shop records its VSQG obligations (and that LQG obligations are *not* applicable). | | **How & When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Monthly** track waste generation (weight or volume) to confirm it remains < 100 kg.
• **Annually** review waste streams, re‑characterize if processes change, and verify VSQG status.
• **After any process change** (e.g., new finishing line), re‑calculate generation rates.
• Conduct a yearly internal audit of waste storage areas, record‑keeping, and ID number validity. | --- ### 4. Complete OSHA 300 Injury & Illness Recordkeeping | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Regulatory Requirement** | Employers must record work‑related injuries/illnesses on OSHA 300 logs, post the annual summary (Feb 1 – Apr 30), and report fatalities/serious incidents to OSHA. | | **Source** | 29 CFR 1904 (OSHA Recordkeeping) | | **Applicability to this Shop** | **Applicable**. Although the shop has only 9 employees (below the 10‑employee **size** exemption), it falls under the **high‑hazard industry** “Wood Product Manufacturing” (NAICS 321). The OSHA recordkeeping rule (§ 1904.1) explicitly states that employers with ≤ 10 employees in high‑hazard industries **must** keep records. | | **Basis for Applicability** | 29 CFR 1904.1(b)(1) & Appendix A (list of high‑hazard industries). | | **ISO Clause** | **ISO 45001:2018 6.1.3** – identify legal & other requirements (OSHA recordkeeping). | | **How & When to Evaluate (9.1.2)** | • **Quarterly** review OSHA 300 entries for completeness and accuracy.
• **Annually** (by Jan 31) compile the previous year’s log, calculate total incident rates, and prepare the summary.
• **Feb 1** post the summary in a conspicuous location until Apr 30.
• **After any serious injury** (hospitalization, amputation, eye loss), report to OSHA within 24 h and evaluate root cause.
• Conduct a yearly internal audit of recordkeeping procedures and training for the person responsible. | --- ### Summary of Compliance Evaluation (ISO 9.1.2) for the Shop | Obligation | Evaluation Frequency | Method | Records to Retain | |------------|----------------------|--------|-------------------| | **SPCC** | Annually + after any storage change | Inventory count, calculation of total gallons | Inventory sheet, compliance register entry | | **Tier II** | Annually + after new chemical introduction | Chemical purchase & usage reconciliation, threshold check | Chemical list, threshold calculation, signed checklist | | **Hazardous‑Waste (VSQG)** | Monthly (generation) + Annually (status) | Weigh/measure waste, review processes, verify ID number | Waste logs, shipping papers, audit report | | **OSHA 300** | Quarterly (log review) + Annual (summary) + Event‑driven (serious incidents) | Review entries, calculate rates, post summary, report to OSHA | OSHA 300 logs, summary sheets, incident reports, audit findings | --- ### Bottom Line for the Shop - **Required now:** OSHA 300 recordkeeping; basic VSQG waste‑management (EPA ID, waste identification, proper disposal, no accumulation > 1,000 kg). - **Not required:** SPCC plan, Tier II reports, full LQG program. - **Cost implication:** The $30,000 quote is **excessive** for the actual regulatory footprint. A realistic budget would cover waste disposal fees, a modest training program, and the administrative time to maintain OSHA logs—typically a few thousand dollars annually, not tens of thousands. By focusing on the **applicable** obligations and implementing a simple compliance‑evaluation schedule (as outlined above), the shop can meet both regulatory and ISO 14001/45001 requirements efficiently.
